薪.meaning: A village keeps a friendly dragon that eats only fresh <part>grass</part>: no hay, just <part>new</part> green stalks. Every morning it munches an armful and breathes fire into the bakery ovens. Grass in, flames out: the farmers are growing its <kanji>fuel</kanji>.
薪.on: A child sits by its warm belly to thaw one frozen <sound>shin</sound>.
薪.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma toasts a <sound>ki</sound>wi on its breath for a snack.

侯.meaning: A pompous noble hangs his velvet cloak on a <part>coat hook</part>, fixes his medals on with a <part>staple</part>, then throws a <part>dart</part> at a map to pick his next castle. He's not a king, not even a duke, but you must bow: he's a <kanji>marquis</kanji>.
侯.on: He eats his ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne with a knife and fork.

桁.meaning: Builders at a busy <part>crossroads</part> want one bridge over all four roads, so they chop the tallest <part>tree</part> in town and lay it from rooftop to rooftop. Cars pass under, cats stroll across the top. The whole junction leans on one <kanji>beam</kanji>.
桁.on: A cat walks the length of it with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in its mouth.
桁.kun: At lunch a builder boils a <sound>ke</sound>ttle and eats a <sound>ta</sound>co up there.

醸.meaning: A grandma keeps her homemade cider in an old <part>dynamite</part> crate hidden under the <part>laundry pile</part>, where it's warm and dark. It bubbles and fizzes and now and then pops its cork. All her shirts smell of apples. She has a strong <kanji>brew</kanji> going.
醸.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of the laundry, hiccupping.
醸.kun: '<sound>Ca</sound>lm down,' she tells it, and wipes the cider off its nose with a <sound>mo</sound>p.

膝.meaning: A fisherman sits under the <part>moon</part> with his back to a <part>tree</part> and an <part>umbrella</part> over his head against the <part>water</part> spraying off the lake. His cat curls up on the only dry spot left, the bend of his leg: his <kanji>knee</kanji>.
膝.on: When the rain gets worse he throws a bed <sound>sheet</sound> over them both.
膝.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>, hu<sound>zzah</sound>!' he cheers when a fish bites, and the cat doesn't budge.

捗.meaning: A diver who can't swim clips an <part>anchor</part> to her belt and goes for a <part>walk</part> along the seabed, one heavy step at a time, towards a sunken ship. Fish zip in rings around her, but every step counts: slow, steady <kanji>progress</kanji>.
捗.on: Her reward inside the wreck: a sealed tin of <sound>choc</sound>olate.
捗.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, staying <sound>ca</sound>lm as a <sound>do</sound>lphin tows her the last bit.

謎.meaning: An old owl leads hikers <part>astray</part> with one short <part>speech</part>: 'What has roots nobody sees and stands taller than trees?' They wander in circles thinking until dark, and only when they answer does the path appear. The owl lives on a <kanji>riddle</kanji>.
謎.on: The forest paths twist round its tree like a hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze.
謎.kun: The last hiker shares her <sound>na</sound>an with a lost <sound>zo</sound>mbie who's been stuck on it for years.

訟.meaning: A man slips on a banana peel in a <part>public</part> park, stands up and gives a furious <part>speech</part> to the crowd, pointing at the banana. Then he hires a lawyer and takes it to court. Nobody has ever tried to <kanji>sue</kanji> a fruit before.
訟.on: The trial becomes the best <sound>show</sound> in town.

穫.meaning: A <part>falconer</part> sends his hawk circling over the fields of <part>grain</part>, not to hunt but to scare off the crows. The farmers cut the golden stalks in peace while it wheels overhead. Not one ear stolen this year: the best <kanji>harvest</kanji> yet.
穫.on: The hawk's reward is a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass from the farm's soup pot.
